newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SHK Prop posts slow 95/96 but improvement seen.
newsitem.headline: SHK Prop posts slow 95/96 but improvement seen.

text.p: Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd reported weak earnings growth in its 1995/96 financial year on Wednesday, hurt by a slowdown in industrial property sales, but analysts expected an improvement in the current fiscal year.

The property investment and development company reported net profit for the year ended June 30 of HK$11.04 billion (US$1.42 billion) compared to HK$10.36 billion the previous year, up 6.5 percent, giving earnings per share of HK$4.69 versus HK$4.46.
"This is the lowest growth rate ever recorded over the last four or five years," said Edward Chan, research director at NAVA SC Securities. He had expected a 7.7 percent rise in earnings.
Chan said between 1992 and 1995, Sun Hung Kai Properties posted average earnings per share growth of about 25 percent, while for 1995/96 it was only five percent.
"The results are within market expectation," said Desmond Cheung, an associate director at Vickers Ballas.
He had expected net profit of HK$11.08 billion.
But both analysts and the company itself predicted an improvement in 1996/97.
"Barring unforseen circumstances, the group's results for the coming year will show a satisfactory improvement," Sun Hung Kai Properties said in a statement.

The company said that during 1995/96, total property sales generated by the group, both as principal and as agent, amounted to HK$15.38 billion, up 14 percent compared with the previous year. It said gross rental income for the year ended June 30 totalled HK$4.40 billion, up nine percent.
Analysts said a weak industrial property sector had hampered growth.
"The industrial property sector was not strong," said Manfred Ho, senior research analyst at CEF GC Brokerage Ltd.
"We are still seeing sluggish sales in this division. The company was forced to hold onto some of the properties and shift them into their investment property portfolio, he said.

Sun Hung Kai Properties said in a statement it had completed 1.5 million square feet of industrial and industrial office properties, but had retained about one million square feet of industrial premises for rental.
"That is why they registered a mediocre performance in fiscal year 1996," said Chan.
But he said over the next two years Sun Hung Kai Properties was expected to take advantage of a strong recovery in the residential property market.
Sun Hung Kai Properties said the majority of its sites under development are large scale residential projects in new major towns in Hong Kong's New Territories.

"They will increase their developmental area for residential sectors from 3.2 million square feet in 1996 to about 4.3 to 4.4 million square feet in 1997 and 1998 and I think this will help bring back EPS growth to the 20 to 24 percent level over the next two years," said Chan.
He forecast earnings per share growth of 20.3 percent in fiscal 1997 and 24 percent in fiscal 1998.

Ho said he was expecting 20 percent growth in net profit for fiscal year 1997, with luxury residential properties at Royal Ascot phase II, King's Park and East Point City the major contributors to earnings.
Cheung was also optimistic, predicting net profit of HK$15 billion in fiscal 1997.
Sun Hung Kai Properties shares closed HK$0.75 lower at HK$81.75 on Wednesday before the release of the earnings. (US$1=HK$7.8)
